notes: τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν and ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ both empty their article under rule 20 proper, while τὴν χεῖρα takes *thy* on the article under rule 20's second arm — the difference is whether a pronoun stands to carry it.
*round about* and *forth* (twice) realize the περι-, ἐκ- and ἐξ- preverbs and stay inside their verbs' units under rule 106.

περιβλεψάμενος αὐτούς → *looked round about on them* puts the supplied *on* with the accusative pronoun as the mark of the verb's government; rule 106's dative/genitive clause does not reach an accusative, so reading *look round about on* as one phrasal verb remains defensible.
